analysis.title: GOAL Kickstart: Tech wreck - rotation out of AI stocks continues into midterm elections
key_insights: Global AI-linked stocks sold off sharply last week on concerns about AI capex, monetisation and disruption. Nasdaq is down 9% from its October peak and underperformed the S&P equal-weight index by 12%.
US Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth is tracking 33% y/y, but momentum is slowing.
This week's focus is the US midterm elections, US labour market data, and European central bank meetings, inflation and PMIs.
Risk appetite fell in October amid several risk-off rotations across and within assets. The GS Risk Appetite Indicator (RAI) fell to -0.5 on Friday.
The rotation from AI-related stocks into non-AI areas has been sharp. The S&P 500 low vol index outperformed by 17% in October, one of its strongest relative monthly returns since the Tech bubble.
Tech dominance in equity benchmarks raises the benefit of style diversification and of exposures less correlated with AI stocks. Nasdaq vs low vol has tracked AI vs ex-AI stocks this year.

The S&P 500 low vol index has been negatively correlated with Nasdaq since the summer. This negative-beta dynamic has kept the VIX relatively anchored, and implied S&P 500 correlation is unusually low given the decline in 'Global Growth' pricing.
AI risk has dominated cyclical risk: Nasdaq implied vol has risen sharply relative to Russell 2000 implied vol.
Unlike the summer momentum sell-off, when semiconductors led the risk-off, last week Hyperscaler implied vol rose around results before resetting.
Markets are pricing elevated event risk around the next NVIDIA results. The implied S&P 500 move is comparable to that around the US midterm elections.
GS stays overweight equities for 3m/12m. The valuation de-rating plus slowing but still good earnings growth should give lower but still attractive risk-adjusted returns.
Near peak nominal growth, inflation and hawkishness, GS expects rates to stabilise so bonds can buffer equities more. GS recently upgraded bonds to OW for 12m.
On the 3m horizon GS is neutral bonds and overweight cash, because AI concerns, midterm elections and Middle East tensions could drive more volatility with limited bond buffer.

GS sees three paths to a rebound in risk appetite: (1) easing AI concerns with more evidence on monetisation, (2) rates relief helped by falling energy prices and easing Middle East tensions, (3) a larger RAI decline below -1, which improves the asymmetry for adding risk into year-end.
The passage of time could also help as event risks such as the midterm elections clear.

GS cross-asset forecasts: S&P 500 7580 now, 8000 at 3m, 8300 at 6m, 8700 at 12m. US 10y yield 4.91% now, 4.72% at 3m, 4.43% at 12m. Gold $3,896 now, $4,715 at 3m, $5,235 at 12m. WTI $108 now, $90 at 3m, $72 at 12m.

GS equity allocation: OW S&P 500, MSCI Asia-Pacific ex Japan and Topix; UW Stoxx Europe 600. Bonds: US, Germany and UK 10y OW at 12m (UK and US neutral at 3m), Japan UW. Commodities neutral except gold OW.

sector_views.rationale: AI-linked stocks are in a sharp rotation on capex, monetisation and disruption concerns. GS sees a rebound path through more evidence on AI monetisation but keeps equities OW overall.

The S&P 500 low vol index outperformed by 17% in October and is negatively correlated with Nasdaq, offering diversification away from AI stocks. GS frames this as a style-diversification benefit rather than a formal rating.

GS expects slowing but still good earnings growth, which together with the valuation de-rating supports lower but still attractive risk-adjusted equity returns.
Implied S&P 500 move around the next NVIDIA results is similar in size to the move implied for the US midterm elections.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields are at a high percentile of the 10-year range (98th). GS expects rates to stabilise near peak nominal growth, inflation and hawkishness.

GS expects a large decline in oil, which would give rates relief and help risk appetite.
Falling energy prices are one of the paths to a rebound in risk appetite.

tension_points.theme: AI stock rotation vs equity overweight
tension_points.bull_case: Valuation de-rating plus slowing but still good earnings growth (Q3 S&P 500 EPS tracking +33% y/y) should deliver lower but still attractive risk-adjusted returns. Rates should stabilise near peak nominal growth, inflation and hawkishness, so bonds can buffer equities more.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex, monetisation and disruption concerns have driven a 9% Nasdaq drawdown from the October peak. AI concerns, midterm elections and Middle East tensions could drive more volatility over 3m with limited buffer from bonds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deeper RAI decline below -1 would improve the asymmetry to add risk. The bull case rebuilds on easing AI concerns with more evidence on monetisation, rates relief, or clearing of event risks such as the midterm elections.
